nodes.speaker: aria
nodes.text: Welcome to Artemis Base, Commander. Every choice costs resources and time. Hold on until Day 84 for crew rotation. Drag me left or right.
nodes.fact: The lunar south pole is a top target for bases: sunlit peaks plus ice hidden in shadowed craters.

nodes.speaker: arch
nodes.text: Setup day: where do we put the solar array?

variants.text: Our ridge sees the Sun almost all month. A tall mast array could catch every last ray.
The crater edge is shadowy, and the Sun only peeks over the rim. Where do we put the solar array?

nodes.fact: Near the poles the Sun sits low on the horizon and casts long shadows, so panels on tall masts catch sunlight longer.

nodes.speaker: sci
nodes.text: Setup day: ice hides in a permanently shadowed crater. Send the rover, or drill nearby soil?

variants.text: Setup day: the ice crater is right next to base! Send the rover, or drill nearby soil?
Setup day: the ice is a long drive from our ridge. Send the rover, or drill nearby soil?

nodes.fact: NASA's LCROSS mission crashed a rocket stage into a polar crater in 2009 and found water in the plume.
